the_rotary_tribe.description: Rotary owners form one of the most dedicated and knowledgeable automotive communities worldwide
characteristics: Deep technical knowledge about their engines
Willingness to accept quirks others find unacceptable
Strong community bonds and mutual support
unwritten_rules: Never talk badly about someone's apex seals
Always wave to other RX-7/RX-8 drivers
Premix is not optional, it's essential
Rev it before you shut it off

the_warmup.practice: Never shut off a cold rotary engine
the_warmup.reason: Prevents flooding and ensures proper oil distribution

the_cooldown.reason: Allows turbo oil drain, prevents hot spots
the_cooldown.turbo_specific: Even more critical on turbo rotaries

the_redline_ritual.practice: Rev to redline at least once per week
the_redline_ritual.reason: Clears carbon deposits from ports and apex seals
the_redline_ritual.technique: Full throttle pulls when engine is warm

premixing.belief: Supplements MOP for apex seal longevity

the_dipstick_check.practice: Check oil at every fuel stop

terminology.apex_seals: The equivalent of piston rings - critical sealing element
terminology.dorito: Slang for the triangular rotor (Reuleaux triangle shape)
terminology.e_shaft: Eccentric shaft - rotary equivalent of crankshaft
terminology.flooding: When engine won't start due to excess fuel (common when cold)
terminology.rew: Rotary Engine Wankel - specific to twin-turbo 13B
terminology.peripheral_port: Ports in rotor housing (not side housing)
terminology.street_port: Mild port enlargement for power gains
terminology.MOP: Metering Oil Pump - injects oil to apex seals
terminology.chatter_marks: Irregular wear patterns on housings (the problem Mazda solved)

myth_1.truth: Properly maintained rotaries can last 150,000+ miles
myth_1.caveat: Neglect and abuse cause premature failure

myth_2.truth: 15-22 MPG typical - not great, but not catastrophic

myth_3.context: Owners who maintain properly have excellent reliability

myth_4.myth: You can't daily drive a rotary
myth_4.truth: Many owners daily drive RX-7s and RX-8s

myth_5.truth: Renesis more prone; REW and earlier less so

sevenstock.description: Largest RX-7 gathering in the world
sevenstock.activities: Car show, vendor row, track day, dyno competition

local_meets.finding: Search Facebook groups, forums for local events

why_rotary_owners_are_different: The engine demands attention - owners must understand it
Unique driving experience creates visceral connection
Being different from mainstream is part of identity
Successfully maintaining a rotary brings pride
The sound is unlike anything else on the road
common_sentiments: Once you go rotary, you never go back
It's not just a car, it's a lifestyle
The extra maintenance is worth it for the experience

opportunities: 8C range extender introduces rotary to new generation
community_response: Extensive parts hoarding and sharing networks
Training programs for new rotary mechanics
